# client-sf-oauth

> Get a Salesforce access token from Node.js with OAuth 2.0 — JWT bearer, web-server (authorization code) with PKCE, or username-password — in TypeScript with typed parameters. The package obtains the token; it does not call the Salesforce data APIs, refresh tokens, or manage sessions. It moves credentials, so every constructor validates before I/O, hosts must be `https:`, secrets travel only in request bodies, and thrown errors are redacted.

## Purpose and flow selection

- Use `SF_JWTConnect` for a backend service, scheduled job, CLI, or integration with no user present: a certificate registered on the Connected App replaces any password (grant `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`).
- Use `SF_WebAppConnect` when a user logs in through a browser: the web server (authorization code) flow with PKCE `S256`, which Salesforce requires by default on Connected Apps created since Winter '23. The authorize step and the callback are two HTTP requests; persist `codeVerifier` and `state` per user session between them.
- `SF_PassConnect` (username-password grant) is deprecated: Salesforce is retiring the grant and it is disabled on new orgs. It remains functional and is not scheduled for removal from the library.

## Install and runtime

- `npm install client-sf-oauth`
- Node.js `>=20`. CommonJS build (`main: dist/index.js`) with bundled declarations (`types: dist/index.d.ts`). No `exports` map, no ESM build.
- Named imports work from TypeScript compiled to CommonJS (`import { SF_JWTConnect } from 'client-sf-oauth'`) and from CommonJS JavaScript (`const { SF_JWTConnect } = require('client-sf-oauth')`). From native ESM (`.mjs` or `"type": "module"`) use the default export and destructure it: `import pkg from 'client-sf-oauth'; const { SF_JWTConnect } = pkg;` — named ESM imports fail in 0.7.x (`Named export 'SF_JWTConnect' not found`) because the package is CommonJS-only with no `exports` map.
- Runtime dependencies: `axios`, `jsonwebtoken`.

## Exports

The entry point exports exactly seven names. Signatures as emitted in `dist/index.d.ts` for 0.7.x:

```text
class SF_JWTConnect
  constructor(parameters: JWTParameters)
  createJWT(passphrase?: string): string
  requestAccessToken(jwt: string): Promise<AxiosResponse>
  createJWTAndGetAccessToken(passphrase?: string): Promise<AxiosResponse>

class SF_WebAppConnect
  constructor(parameters: WebAuthCodeParameters)
  get codeVerifier(): string | undefined
  requestAuthCode(): Promise<string>                      // resolves to the URL to redirect the user's browser to
  requestAccessTokenWithCode(code: string, codeVerifier?: string): Promise<AxiosResponse>

class SF_PassConnect  (@deprecated)
  constructor(parameters: PassParameters)
  requestAccessToken(): Promise<AxiosResponse>

interface JWTParameters        { clientId: string; username: string; secret: string; secretText?: boolean; expiration?: number; environment?: string }
interface WebAppParameters     { clientId: string; clientSecret: string; host: string; redirectURI: string }
interface WebAuthCodeParameters extends WebAppParameters { scope?: string; state?: string; immediate?: boolean; code_challenge?: string; code_challenge_method?: string; code_verifier?: string; display?: string; login_hint?: string; nonce?: string; prompt?: string }
interface PassParameters       { clientId: string; clientSecret: string; username: string; password: string; usertoken: string; host: string }
```

- `JWTParameters.secret` is a path to the PEM private key, or the key text itself when `secretText: true`. `expiration` is epoch seconds (default now + 3600). `environment: 'dev'` targets `https://test.salesforce.com`; otherwise `https://login.salesforce.com`.
- Every token method resolves to the `AxiosResponse` of `services/oauth2/token`. The Salesforce JSON is `response.data` (typed `any` in 0.7.x) with `access_token`, `instance_url`, `id`, `token_type`, `issued_at`, `signature`, and `scope`. Never log `response.data` whole.
- Minimal JWT bearer use: `new SF_JWTConnect({ clientId, username, secret })` then `await client.createJWTAndGetAccessToken(passphrase?)`.
- Minimal web server use: request 1 — `const client = new SF_WebAppConnect({ host, clientId, clientSecret, redirectURI, state }); const redirectTo = await client.requestAuthCode(); save { state, codeVerifier: client.codeVerifier } in the user's session`. Request 2 — verify `query.state` equals the saved `state` and delete it (single use), then `await new SF_WebAppConnect({ host, clientId, clientSecret, redirectURI }).requestAccessTokenWithCode(query.code, savedCodeVerifier)`.

## Error contract

- Every thrown message starts with `client-sf-oauth:`. No error carries the request body, URL, headers, or a `cause`.
- Network failures throw an `Error` with `status?: number`, `error?: string` (Salesforce `error`, e.g. `invalid_grant`), `errorDescription?: string`, and `code?: string` (transport code such as `ECONNREFUSED`).
- Invalid constructor input throws before any network or filesystem access with `field: string` naming the parameter; the value is never echoed. A non-object `parameters` argument or a malformed PKCE verifier throws a `TypeError`.
- The classes `OAuthRequestError` and `InvalidParameterError` are not exported from the entry point in 0.7.x: match on `message.startsWith('client-sf-oauth:')` and the properties above, not on `instanceof`.
- Log `error.message` only; never the error object.
